eyebrow: A harder kind of ML problem

steps.label: Financial returns
steps.sub: R-squared under 2% can be a strong model

code:
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score

model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
preds = model.predict(X_test)

r2 = r2_score(y_test, preds)
print(f"Out-of-sample R^2: {r2:.4f}")
# 0.01 to 0.02 is often genuinely strong
caption: An out-of-sample R-squared of 0.01-0.02 on next-period returns is often a strong, usable result.
